notes: DID_sample rebuilt in R from main_code.do lines 106-117 (base_reg.dta merged m:1 to IPO_shock.dta on state-year, keep matched; year_effective = first year with ipo_shock==1 within the merged sample; post = year>=year_effective, 0 for never-shocked states). Households are a repeated cross-section (one row per h_id) assigned to 40 states; years 1987, 1988, 1991, 1993, 1995-2003 (13 survey years). Cohorts 1987 (3 states, treated from the first sample year = always-treated), 1991 (2), 1993 (7), 1995 (1), 1996 (2), 2001 (1); 24 never-treated states; post is absorbing by construction. Controls $x1 (9 household-level, 2 state-level) entered linearly as published; hhead_education is a 1-3 rank entered linearly by the authors, so it is kept numeric. Published coefficient from the authors' results/table4a.rtf (no article text or PDF in the project); SE derived from the reported t statistic; R/fixest reproduces coefficient and t exactly. in_abstract_intro unknown (no article text); the DiD is a robustness exercise for the continuous local-agglomeration regressor.
